acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Mummies family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Husk, T1, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Loose-End Grasp Initiate (Initiate) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two earth construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: A dried human husk in crude grey head-to-foot bandages, one dragging leg, empty eye holes, exposed flesh in several gaps, and one extra-long loose strip tied at the hip.

Signature mechanic: Common-Grave Draw: the Husk advances on one dragging leg while a grey bandage end trails from its hip; when the arms lift, the end loops around the nearest ankle line and retracts toward the hip knot.
battlefieldDuty: Probe footwork by dragging one crude wrapping end behind a stiff advance, then pulling the strip into a short ankle snare before the exposed knot can be retied.
constructionDimensions: Earth affinity is distinguished from ordinary tomb sand by structural mineralization: compressed sandstone splints under linen, load-bearing lapis joints, crystal scarab clasps, and carved stone channels on masks, armor, or sarcophagus lids.
Stance and attacks become masonry-driven through keyed foot sockets, settling plates, pale fractures at wrapped joints, and localized blocks rising only along a visible carved channel.
counterplay: Step over or pin the strip before it retracts, then cut the visible hip knot; the Husk must stop and rewrap the gap before it can snare again. Affinity signal: A load-bearing lapis clasp or sandstone splint turns chalk-white after a committed step or bind; breaking it releases the linen tension and collapses the connected structure.
forbiddenTreatments: Palette-only earth treatment or extra tan sand without structural mineralization and changed load paths
Glow-only earth treatment without a fracture, clasp, or masonry joint
Pasted rocks that hide wrapping logic, glyphs, masks, or human silhouette
Ordinary family-native tomb dust mislabeled as Earth affinity
identityInvariants: A stiff-limbed human or humanoid silhouette remains wrapped from head to foot, with arms held forward, crossed, guarding, inscribing, or commanding through readable linen tension.
Sun-bleached linen, sand beige, desert ochre, deep gold, lapis blue, and turquoise remain funerary materials and symbols rather than affinity colors.
Linen bandage, dried flesh, gold leaf, lapis, carnelian, bronze, and sandstone grave goods stay materially distinct and retain visible knots, stitches, glyph routes, and breakable seals.
Family-native sand and dust follow disturbed wrappings, tomb movement, and burial objects without becoming Earth or Wind affinity by themselves.
Escalation adds precious thread, glyph density, collars, masks, armor, headdresses, and sarcophagus regalia while the bandages never come off and always explain binding and counterplay.
telegraph: Empty eye holes face down, both stiff arms rise, and the dirty trailing strip straightens from the dragging leg to its hip knot.
